rules.rule: Report n after each step. (1) Start with all examse records (2,596). (2) Keep MEC second exams: PERTECH not blank (1,859); drop home second exams (HXRRDAYS not blank, 737). (3) Link exam.sas with DMPSTAT=2 and MXPAXTMR not blank (MEC visit 1). (4) Keep ages 30-79 at visit 1: 360 <= MXPAXTMR <= 959. (5) Exclude prior MI (HAF10=1), stroke (HAC1D=1) or CHF (HAC1C=1). (6) Exclude pregnancy at either visit (MAPF12R=1 or MARF12R=1). (7) Require determinable history (HAF10, HAC1D, HAC1C not 8 or 9). (8) Require complete inputs at BOTH visits: SBP, TC, HDL, serum creatinine, UACR, plus sex, diabetes, current smoking, antihypertensive use and statin use. Tabulate which input is binding for each person lost at step 8. The count is unweighted: the second exam has no weights and NCHS advises against using design variables with it.
rules.source: Merged from all four domain maps; EXAMSE-acc.pdf p.149; LABSE-acc.pdf pp.10-11

rules.topic: MEC vs home second exam (FINAL, disagreement resolved)
rules.rule: A MEC second exam is examse PERTECH (cols 258-262) not blank, n=1,859; equivalently HXRRDAYS (3733-3735) blank. A home second exam is HXRRDAYS not blank, n=737, and is excluded. Do NOT use MXRRDAYS-not-blank (n=1,854): it misses 5 MEC exams with a blank interval (SEQN 01937, 04794, 06124, 08777, 09786). Do not use labse MXRSESSR either, since it is filled for all 2,596 records. Re-checked this session: the EXAMSE-acc p.149 PERTECH counts sum to 1,618 + 241 = 1,859 non-blank and 737 blank; PERLEVEL shows the same split; HXRRDAYS has 1,859 blank.
rules.source: examse.sas INPUT lines 2623-2624, 4214, 4217; EXAMSE-acc.pdf p.149, p.768, p.769, p.772

rules.rule: TCR, HDR, CER and GHR are filled for home second exams, while UBR, URR and PER6 BP are not. Lab completeness alone never proves a MEC visit, so always apply the PERTECH filter first. Requiring valid PER6 SBP and UBR/URR excludes home exams anyway.
rules.source: LABSE-acc.pdf pp.83-87 (Appendix 1), p.68; EXAMSE-acc.pdf p.126

rules.rule: Read each .dat line by line. Strip CR/LF, then right-pad to the file's last column (adult 3346, exam 6233, lab 1977, examse 4470, labse 693): lab.dat, exam.dat and adult.dat appear to have trailing blanks trimmed, so never read fixed-size byte chunks. Columns are 1-based inclusive, so Python slice = line[start-1:end]. Take each field as text and check it before converting: all spaces = blank; a string of 8s exactly as wide as the field = blank but applicable; 9s of field width only where documented (questionnaire DK). Then convert the stripped text to float, honouring the embedded decimal point and applying no implied decimals: CER '0001' = 1.0; UBR '00160' = 160; UBP '015700' = 15700. Expect 20,050 records in adult.dat, 31,311 in exam.dat, 29,314 in lab.dat and 2,596 each in examse.dat and labse.dat.
rules.source: SAS INPUT/FORMAT blocks; labse/examse spot-checks by earlier agents; file sizes vs LRECL

rules.rule: 8-fill (8, 88, 888, 8888, 88888, 888888 by width) = blank but applicable = missing. Blank = not applicable or skipped, but in LABSE blank ALSO marks eligible persons with no result: CER has no 8-fill, and URR/UBR use blank for about 214 MEC examinees but 88888 for only 1. So treat blank and 8-fill alike as missing for every lab input. Treat questionnaire 9 = DK as missing unless a rule below says otherwise. These are NOT missing: K5=000; URP/URR 007.9 and UBP/UBR 0000.4/000.4 (below-detection fills; see the UACR rule); pupremed HQRXCODE 0088; HQKX2B values 8 and 9.
rules.source: LABSE-acc.pdf p.23, p.62, p.68; lab-acc.pdf pp.82-96; pupremed.pdf pp.45-49

rules.rule: Primary: age at the visit-1 MEC exam, from exam.sas MXPAXTMR (1236-1239); eligible if 360 <= MXPAXTMR <= 959. Age at visit 2 (for eGFR) = (MXPAXTMR + MXRRDAYS/30.4375)/12. If MXRRDAYS is 888 or blank (129 MEC exams), use the visit-1 age. Flag anyone whose visit-2 age reaches 80 (960 months or more). Sensitivity: adult.sas HSAGEIR (cols 18-19, NOT 16-17) between 30 and 79. Neither second-exam file has an age or sex variable.
rules.source: exam.sas line 3055; adult.sas line 1399; exam-acc.pdf p.124, p.135; EXAMSE-acc.pdf p.768

rules.rule: Visit-1 SBP = mean of the valid readings among PEP6G1, PEP6H1 and PEP6I1 (exam.sas). Visit-2 SBP = mean of the valid readings among PER6G1, PER6H1 and PER6I1 (examse.sas). A reading is valid if it is a 3-digit numeric value that is not '888' and not blank; judge validity from the SBP field itself, not from the refusal flags. Primary: at least 1 valid reading at EACH visit. Also report counts with at least 2 and with all 3 at both visits. Apply the same rule at both visits. NHANES III supplies no MEC-only average.
rules.source: exam-acc.pdf pp.138-139, pp.171-172; EXAMSE-acc.pdf pp.88-89, pp.126-128

rules.rule: Never use PEPMNK1R/PEPMNK5R/PEPNOK1R (exam.sas), PERMNK1R/PERMNK5R (examse.sas) or HAZMNK1R/HAZMNK5R (adult.sas). Each mixes up to 3 household readings with up to 3 MEC readings and falls back to household-only readings. The household BP was taken once, before visit 1, so these averages are not independent visit-2 values (e.g. SEQN 09786: all PER6 = 888 but PERMNK1R = 109).
rules.source: EXAMSE-acc.pdf p.152; exam-acc.pdf p.173, p.193; ADULT-acc.pdf p.390, p.433

rules.rule: Use the reference-method values: TCP and HDP (lab.sas) at visit 1, TCR and HDR (labse.sas) at visit 2. Do not use CHP or CHR. A value is valid if it is not 888 and not blank. PREVENT uses non-HDL-C = TC - HDL. NHANES III has no correction equation for lipids. Both visits used the same protocols.
rules.source: lab-acc.pdf p.82-83, p.112; LABSE-acc.pdf p.55, p.70, pp.10-11

rules.rule: IDMS-standardized creatinine (mg/dL) = 0.960 x raw - 0.184. Apply it to CEP (visit 1) before CKD-EPI 2021; NCHS 'highly recommends' this (Deming regression, n=190, r=0.978, CCF Roche enzymatic). Applying the same equation to CER (visit 2) is an assumption: LABSE-acc has no such note, but CER came from the same biochemistry profile and same survey protocols. The equation is linear, so a between-visit difference d becomes 0.960 d. Caveat: it was derived in persons aged 60+ and is extrapolated to low values (CER 0.5 maps to 0.296). Completeness only needs a valid creatinine (CEP not 8888/blank; CER not blank).
rules.source: lab-acc.pdf pp.111-112; LABSE-acc.pdf (no note); Selvin 2007 AJKD doi:10.1053/j.ajkd.2007.08.020; Coresh 2002 AJKD doi:10.1053/ajkd.2002.32765

rules.rule: CKD-EPI 2021 is race-free, so race (DMARETHN/DMARACER) is NOT needed. Its inputs are calibrated creatinine, sex (HSSEX) and age at each visit. The count does not compute eGFR. Completeness = valid creatinine plus known sex and age.
rules.source: Analytic design (CKD-EPI 2021)

rules.rule: UACR (mg/g) = 100 x albumin (ug/mL) / urine creatinine (mg/dL): UBP/URP at visit 1, UBR/URR at visit 2. Keep the albumin below-detection fill (UBP '0000.4', UBR '000.4') as the value 0.4 (LOD/sqrt2). Primary: a urine creatinine below-detection fill (URP/URR '007.9', meaning any value under 10 mg/dL) makes UACR not reliably computable, so count it as incomplete. Report how many are lost this way, and give a sensitivity count that keeps 7.9. Treat 888888/88888 and blank as missing. Urine was collected only in the MEC.
rules.source: lab-acc.pdf p.29, p.96, p.123, p.130; LABSE-acc.pdf p.68, p.81, p.88, p.90

rules.rule: Statin = 1 if the SEQN has any pupremed row with HQRXCODE in {1664 lovastatin, 3064 pravastatin, 3088 simvastatin}; RXDDRGID {d00280, d00348, d00746} gives the same set. Statin = 0 if the SEQN has no pupremed row (non-user) or has rows but no statin code. Statin = UNKNOWN for the 91 persons whose HQKX1B=8 rows are entirely fill: primary treats them as incomplete; sensitivity sets statin = 0. A further 21 persons have an unidentified drug for ICD-9 272.x; they stay statin = 0 in the primary analysis and are flagged for sensitivity. There is no fluvastatin code, and drug class 0912 is NOT statin-specific. Note that adult.dat HAX1B/HAX2B are blank for everyone, so pupremed is the only drug-name source.
rules.source: pupremed.xpt (pyreadstat); pupremed.pdf Appendix 1 pp.20/25/26, p.10; ADULT-acc.pdf pp.327-328

rules.rule: Sensitivity statin proxy: adult HAE9D=1 (any prescribed cholesterol medicine), or any pupremed class 0912. Blank HAE9D because a gate was negative (HAE6=2, HAE7=2 or HAE8D=2) = not treated. Treating the gate DK answers (HAE6=9 n=712, HAE7=9, HAE8D=9) as not treated is an assumption.
rules.source: ADULT-acc.pdf pp.180-183; pupremed.pdf Appendix 2 p.28

rules.rule: Treated = HAE5A=1. Not treated: HAE1=5 (HAE2 blank), HAE2=2, HAE4A=2 or HAE5A=2. HAE2=9 (n=42 overall) and HAE4A=9 (n=4) skip HAE5A; primary codes them as not treated (assumption, flag them), sensitivity as missing. Missing: HAE5A=8, or any path that ends on an 8 code with no later answer. HAE2=8 and HAE4A=8 continue, so use the downstream answer. HAE4D is NOT a medication item. Sensitivity: also count as treated anyone with pupremed class 0506, 0507, 0510, 0512, 0513 or 0514 in any slot. Carry the status forward to visit 2.
rules.source: ADULT-acc.pdf pp.175-178; pupremed.pdf Appendix 2 pp.27-28

rules.rule: Self-reported diabetes (SRD) = 1 if HAD1 is 1 or 8 and the person is not gestational-only (gestational-only = HAD3=1 and HAD4=2). SRD = 0 if HAD1=2 or the person is gestational-only. SRD is unknown if HAD1=9, or if HAD1=8 with no treatment answer. Diabetes at visit v = 1 if SRD=1, or HAD6=1, or HAD10=1, or exam-day insulin at that visit (PHPINSU=1 at v1, PHRINSU=1 at v2), or HbA1c at that visit >= 6.5% (GHP at v1, GHR at v2). It = 0 if SRD=0 and no positive criterion. It is missing if SRD is unknown and no criterion is positive. Primary: missing HbA1c does not make diabetes missing. Sensitivity: require a valid HbA1c at both visits to classify diabetes = 0, and add fasting glucose >= 126 when PHxFAST >= 8 h. Diabetes can differ between visits through HbA1c; report how often it does. Blank HAD6/HAD10 = not asked = not treated.
rules.source: ADULT-acc.pdf pp.171-173; lab-acc.pdf p.68, p.93; LABSE-acc.pdf p.41, p.65

rules.rule: Current smoker (PREVENT input) = HAR3=1, which requires HAR1 of 1 or 8. Not current = HAR1=2 (never smoker; HAR3 blank by design) or HAR3=2 (former smoker). Missing = HAR3=8. Neither item has a DK code. Carry the status forward to visit 2. Sensitivity: visit-specific smoking from MAPA1 (v1) and MARA1 (v2) > 0 cigarettes in the past 5 days.
rules.source: ADULT-acc.pdf p.289; exam-acc.pdf p.698; EXAMSE-acc.pdf p.682

rules.rule: Exclude if HAF10=1 (MI), HAC1D=1 (stroke) or HAC1C=1 (CHF). If none is 1 but any is 8 or 9, CVD-free status cannot be confirmed: primary counts the person as incomplete, and reports how many. Note that HAF10=8 is large overall (286).
rules.source: ADULT-acc.pdf p.157, pp.187-188

rules.rule: The household questionnaire has no doctor-diagnosed angina or CHD item; the only CHD diagnosis is HAF10 (MI). The Rose site criterion (HAF7A-H) cannot be coded because the anatomy drawing is not available locally. Primary therefore excludes on MI, stroke and CHF only. Sensitivity 1: also exclude Rose exertional chest pain without the site criterion, i.e. HAF1=1 AND (HAF2=1 OR HAF3=1) AND HAF4=1 AND HAF5=1 AND HAF6=1. HAF4=3 is never Rose angina. Sensitivity 2: also exclude pupremed users of class 0503 (antianginals) or 0508 (coronary vasodilators).
rules.source: ADULT-acc.pdf pp.184-187, note p.416; pupremed.pdf Appendix 2

rules.rule: Exclude if MAPF12R=1 (visit 1, exam.sas col 5151) or MARF12R=1 (visit 2, examse.sas col 3385). Men and women 60+ are blank by design and are not pregnant. For women 30-59, codes 8, 9 or blank mean pregnancy status is unknown: primary keeps them (pregnancy is an exclusion, not a PREVENT input) and reports how many; sensitivity excludes them. Do not use PEPPREG/PERPREG (BIA screen) or adult HAD3/HAM15K.
rules.source: exam-acc.pdf p.713, pp.730-731; EXAMSE-acc.pdf pp.699-700, pp.718-719, p.155

rules.rule: There was no second household interview and no second prescription file. Smoking, antihypertensive use, statin use, self-reported diabetes and CVD history come only from adult.dat and pupremed, which were collected before visit 1. They are applied unchanged to both visits, which assumes no change over the 1-52 day interval. At visit 2 only HbA1c, exam-day insulin, glucose, pregnancy and past-5-day cigarettes are measured again. Visit-2 MARC7 (and HXRE7, which covers the 737 home exams only) is a yes/no question on any prescription in the past 24 h and cannot identify drug classes.
rules.source: LABSE-acc.pdf pp.3-4, p.11; EXAMSE-acc.pdf p.689, p.740; pupremed.pdf p.2

rules.rule: PREVENT-ASCVD base model inputs: sex, age, total and HDL cholesterol (as non-HDL-C and HDL-C), SBP, diabetes, current smoking, eGFR, antihypertensive use and statin use. UACR enters the add-on (UACR-augmented) model. BMI is not an ASCVD input; it is used in the HF model only. These items define 'complete inputs'.
rules.source: Khan SS et al. Circulation 2024 (PREVENT); recalled, not re-checked in this session

rules.rule: The PREVENT calculator's stated valid ranges are reportedly TC 130-320 mg/dL, HDL 20-100 mg/dL, SBP 90-180 mmHg and eGFR 15-140, with age 30-79. Do not exclude on these ranges in the primary completeness count. Optionally report how many complete cases fall outside them at either visit. Verify the ranges against the PREVENT supplement before using them.
rules.source: Not verified in this session

rules.rule: LABSE says the second exam used the same protocols, the same MEC staff and the same period as visit 1. It does not name laboratories for TCR, HDR, CER, UBR or URR. HbA1c at both visits was measured at the University of Missouri-Columbia (Diamat HPLC, DCCT-standardized). The NHANES III urine creatinine instrument is disputed in secondary sources (Hitachi 737 at White Sands vs Beckman Synchron); both are Jaffe methods.
rules.source: LABSE-acc.pdf pp.10-11, pp.72-73; Wilhelm-Leen 2009 Am J Med; Shafi 2012 BMC Nephrol

notes:
I merged the four verified domain maps (second exam, first exam and lab, questionnaire, medications and calibration) into the final map above.

Positions: I re-checked every needed column position this session by grepping the INPUT statements of examse.sas, labse.sas, exam.sas, lab.sas and adult.sas. All of them match the verified maps. pupremed.xpt is a SAS transport file, so its variables have no column positions (start=end=0).

How I resolved the disagreements:
1. MEC second-exam flag. The second-exam verifier and the questionnaire verifier disagreed. I re-read the EXAMSE-acc.pdf p.149 codebook. PERTECH is filled for 1,859 records (1,618 examiner codes plus 241 records coded 88888) and blank for 737. PERLEVEL shows the same 1,859/737 split, and HXRRDAYS is blank for exactly 1,859 records. Final rule: PERTECH not blank is the MEC flag (n=1,859). MXRRDAYS is used only for the days between visits; using it as the flag would drop 5 MEC exams (SEQN 01937, 04794, 06124, 08777, 09786).
2. PHRINSU codes. Re-read in LABSE-acc.pdf p.41: 1 = 31, 2 = 1,638, 8 = 926, blank = 1. The medication-domain verifier had 8 and blank swapped.
3. HXRE7. Its counts are 312 + 411 + 14 = 737, which equals the home second-exam count (the same records as HXRLANG and HXRB1). It belongs to the home-exam interview, not to MEC second exams. The medication verifier's claim that 'MARC7 alone drops about a third of visit-2 respondents' is therefore wrong for the MEC cohort.
4. HSAGEIR is at cols 18-19 in adult.sas but 16-17 in exam.sas and lab.sas. MXPAXTMR is at 1236-1239 in exam/lab and 1237-1240 in adult. I chose exam.sas MXPAXTMR (age at the visit-1 MEC exam) as the primary age variable, with adult HSAGEIR as a sensitivity check.
5. GHP applicability (ages 1+ vs 4+) does not matter for ages 30-79.

Analysis choices I made where the maps left options open:
- URP/URR = 7.9 (below detection, meaning creatinine under 10 mg/dL) makes UACR incomplete in the primary count; a sensitivity count keeps those values. Albumin below detection (0.4) is kept as a value.
- The 91 persons whose pupremed records are entirely fill have unknown statin status: incomplete in the primary count, statin = 0 in a sensitivity count.
- Pregnancy with codes 8, 9 or blank among women 30-59 is kept in the primary count and flagged.
- History items coded 8 or 9 with no 'yes' count as incomplete.
- Angina/CHD exclusion is limited to doctor-told MI. Rose exertional angina (without the site criterion) and antianginal drugs are sensitivity exclusions.
- SBP requires at least 1 valid physician reading at each visit; counts with at least 2 and with all 3 are reported too.
- Diabetes is self-report, medication, exam-day insulin, or HbA1c of 6.5% or more at that visit. Missing HbA1c does not make diabetes missing in the primary count.
- Creatinine is IDMS-calibrated with 0.960x - 0.184 at both visits. This is documented for CEP only, so applying it to CER is an assumption.
- CKD-EPI 2021 needs no race variable.
- The count is unweighted.

The PREVENT input-range rule (TC 130-320, HDL 20-100, SBP 90-180, eGFR 15-140) is from memory and is marked unknown; verify it before using it.
